newsitem.title: BELGIUM: GM's Opel Belgium 1996 profit crumbles.
newsitem.headline: GM's Opel Belgium 1996 profit crumbles.

text.p: Opel Belgium, the Antwerp, Belbium-based assembly unit of General Motors Corp., said Monday its net profit fell to 85 million Belgian francs ($2.4 million) in 1996 from 878 million ($25 million) a year earlier despite a 5.7 percent rise in revenue.
It said in a statement that 1996 earnings were strongly influenced by high investment costs and feelings that a real recovery of the Western economy was not materialising.

Spokesman Dirk Snauwaert said the company also made a provision of 638 million francs ($18 million) related to a European Commission ban on Belgian programmes, called Maribel, which allow exporters facing international competition to pay reduced social security contributions.

The commission had ruled that previous Maribel schemes violated EU fair competition rules, but has accepted a new plan which it said involved general measures to preserve blue-collar work rather than sectors.
Snauwaert said the Maribel story would raise eyebrows at the Opel headquarters because it showed there were no steady regulations which made it difficult for Opel to draw up a long-term strategy.
"Hopefully, the Belgian government will work out a solution," he said.
Snauwaert added that the company also suffered from a four-day strike in March 1996.
"Without all this (Maribel and the strike), we would have been at a normal level of profit," Snauwaert said.
Turnover rose to 48.3 billion francs ($1.4 billion) from 45.7 billion ($1.3 billion).
Opel Belgium produced 295,454 cars in 1996, compared with 304,505 in 1995 and 319,000 in 1994. It assembled 182,160 Opel Astras and 113,294 Vectras.
The company has already produced more than 10 million cars.
